context.body: Objects created for royal worship become spoil at the collapse of the kingdom.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem, removes Temple and palace treasures, and cuts up the gold articles Solomon made.
observations.label: Babylon cuts up Solomon’s gold work: action

observations.body: King, court, soldiers, craftsmen, and leaders are carried away while Mattaniah is installed.
observations.label: Babylon cuts up Solomon’s gold work: response

observations.body: treasures · gold vessels Solomon had made · carried away · exile

payload.posture: Read 2 Kings 24:10–17 as later memory and aftermath evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The destruction of Solomon’s work fulfills judgment without making the original dedication unreal.
